Author: @3D-4-U
Content: It's a collection because of the amount of times the waiter served it to you and all those times you ate the food, and its an actual memory, it's different because of the way you see it, and the way its moved around and made. Also, because of who serves it and the heat of the food and the different people trying it. The volume of the video you watch would be different or go up and down differently.And since a food is owned by someone or is owned by tiktok, that could also count as a collection. And the amount of food grains or atoms on that food would still make it a collection. And all the bites you take in the food are different. Everything links to everything in a collection, so actual food can link to food on a screen, making it a collection. I may be thinking about the item differently each time i see/eat it again. You ate it at a different day, or you ate it faster. Also, background noises. Each bite and sound you taste is different. Everything in a single area of the food is different, like the heat or the seasoning. The days or time you try the food in would be different. And if it's one item, I saw it differently each time. Every experience is different, and you need to think about that. And every time you look at the same thing, there's a different way of how you eat/drink it. And the amount of time you left it for or the time of day is different . If 2 groups are the same, join a bigger, different type of group. If those 2 groups are the same, you group it in a bigger category and so on and so on. And I wouldn't like it if I saw the exact same thing twice, that's how you know it's unique. Even if you threw something away or was a past memory, it's still a collection. Every time you eat food, it's a new experience, and that's a difference. You can also have a collection of Tierlist ranking, eg, collection of A+ Rankings, B, C, and so on. And there's a collection of how many times you ate it. Anything you own can count as a collection, and even things you can't own, and your memories too! You learn something new even if it's a similar item. There's such a thing as a collection of duplicates. So all duplicates would be different. It isn't about their lives it's about yours. Moments are collectable whether you notice them or not.

Author: @MaximSraj
Content:
ok, so i actually noted some of these places down and went on the hunt during my recent trip to Paris. Made it to 3 locations, and below are my thoughts: 
1- B.O.U.L.O.M (EUR 1.5): the best among the three, very delicate & has very nice butter feel to it. Though getting to the place is not the easiest as it's pretty far from the normal tourist areas. 
2- Ritz Paris Le Comptoir (EUR 4): the fanciest & most expensive of the bunch, and quite pleasant to eat especially when its still warm. and I see the point of it being more 'dunkable'. And would recommend to go for the pain au chocolat.  
3- Boulangerie Michalak | Poissonnière (EUR 3.9): Joshua has praised the form of the croissant, but now they actually reverted to baking them in the traditional shape. So seems the novelty didn't live long. The croissant is interesting, and a very good one, but comes last among the three in my opinion.

They offered a guarantee  of pure butter to the public by changing the classic shape. So straight croissant are all butter and anything else is suspect.

Content:
Interesting and enjoyable. Re: the cubic doesn’t show the classic honey comb in the video, it doesn’t have the crescent shape which has a historical reason, it maybe outstanding but best croissant?🥐 
As a home baker and croissant maker I can tell you that in a humid environment much of the crisp can be lost quickly. Crisp can also be influenced by amount of egg wash which can make a big difference. It may be more fair to warm them in a 250f oven for a few minutes to re-crisp. Unless of course it’s just under cooked and ment to be taken home and crisped.
French folks have raved about my croissants and even written articles about them. So I really want to go and do the croissant tour to compare and learn. There a lot of bad recipes on the internet. Case in point: the Pain au Chocolate dough recipe on one of the major flour producers website is better than their regular croissant recipe.

Author: @anon_hummus
Content:
Few random infos and thoughts:
1/ Cédric Grolet is a national joke here cause his shop is clearly a tourist trap (the guy's also an asshole apparently). It looks good on TikTok but taste like sh*t and is WAAAYYY too expensive.
2/ French people did not get mad at the crookie, we like when people try stuff with traditionnal foods (we're not Italians, they are the one who get mad)
3/ Many "reinventions" are interesting but fall into so many different categories that they shouldn't be compared for "best croissant" in my opinion. The sweet croissants with fillings are pastries, not viennoiseries. The pretzel croissant sounds amazing but I see it more as something we'd have with a salad for lunch. When you want a croissant, you want a croissant (the filled ones should be compared to pâtisseries like éclairs, tartes, millefeuilles, etc. not croissants).
Also some of them like the hot cocoa filled one or the margharita one are not even croissants. They are pastries filled with stuff.
4/ I think the price should come into account too. Because the price of the baguette and the croissant are really important in France and I feel like they'd really be part of the addiction if you ask a French person what they think.

Content: People make fantastic croissants in most every country in the world (though some bakers may be few and far between in a few countries). I'm really disappointed that you only reviewed Parisian boulangeries. How can you possibly claim to have eaten the best in the world when you have only evaluated one very pretentious city? I've been to France several times and I've never been to Paris. We visit a little village called Pont-en-Royans every so often because we have friends there. The boulangerie there makes all types of fantastic bits, including really good croissant, as well as sweet and savory tarts, really great baguettes and the like. The best thing about a village is that you can order whatever you like a day or two in advance and they will make it for you. Same goes for roasted chicken from the local market. Author: @TinovanderZwan-t5f
Content:
My local baker/snack bar yes he has 2 in 1 he uses a lot of bacon for burger toppings so the end result is a lot of bacon fat and he couldn't do much with it well I suggested making croissants using the bacon fat I said that would be the dream recipe for a ham and cheese croissant so I took some of his bacon fat and dough and I went home to make the bacon fat croissants the process is a multi-day process you have to cure the dough for 24 hours and cool the fat for the same amount of time normal croissants have the butter folded in the dough and in multiple steps, after each step, the dough goes back to cool so fold multiple times then cool and repeat about 10 times.
A butter slab can be rolled and folded into the croissant dough bacon fat can't you have to brush it on the dough after every 2 folds do that 10 times then cool after that roll it flat to about an inch brush on more fat every 2 folds and do that whole process 10 times then cool and after cooling roll the dough out and form your croissants.
A ham and cheese croissant can be made in 2 ways no1 roll in the ham and cheese and bake it with the croissant no2 Par-bake the croissant and remove the ends and stuff the ham and cheese inside and finish the baking I like no1 best but many bakeries go with no2 because its faster.
My baker friend was so impressed with the bacon fat ham and cheese croissant that it became a staple in his shop and, it became a hit!
A third method I showed him was folding in dry aged bacon fat and bacon bits and ham flakes and the ham was Parma ham and the cheese was a Castello-Blue cream cheese as well as baking this one in my offset BBQ smoker it also had a truffle egg wash with smoked red Himalaya salt crystals on top and Parmigiano Reggiano roasted over that, my baker friend loved that one to death! but he said this would be a $30,- croissant!!! I could not sell that! well, go ahead and make that one it will blow your mind!!
